property_summary: For any valid interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true iff interfaceId is type(IERC1155).interfaceId or type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId or supported by super; the mutant returns false for type(IERC1155).interfaceId, violating this.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for this exact interfaceId, violating the requirement.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the mutant drops this check so the return becomes false, violating ERC1155 compliance.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for IERC1155MetadataURI or super, it must also return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the mutant drops this check and returns false.

The supportsInterface function must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId because the contract inherits IERC1155; the mutant drops that check and returns false, violating the claim that supportsInterface is true for that specific interface.

The reference C correctly reports support for the IERC1155MetadataURI interface via supportsInterface, while the buggy version does not; for any interfaceId, supportsInterface should return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when the id equals type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId; the mutant removes this check, causing a false return for that specific id.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if interfaceId matches at least one of the supported interfaces (IERC165, IERC1155, or IERC1155MetadataURI); the mutant removes the IERC1155MetadataURI check, so it returns false for type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId while the original returns true.

For any admissible interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true if and only if interfaceId equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId or type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant falsely returns false for type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId; the buggy version removes this check and returns false for that specific id.
balanceOf must revert for the zero address input, but the mutant returns the stored balance, causing a difference in execution (revert vs. return).

For any valid account (non-zero) and token ID, c.balanceOf returns the stored balance; for the zero address, the correct reference reverts while the buggy version returns the stored balance, so the invariant is that balanceOf must revert when account is address(0).
The balanceOf function must return the actual balance of tokens owned by an account for a given id after minting; the mutant always returns 0, violating this for any minted amount.
For any account and token ID, after minting a quantity, the returned balanceOf must equal the minted quantity, but the mutant always returns 0, violating the equality for any non-zero mint.
For any address and token id, after minting a non-zero quantity, balanceOf must return a value strictly greater than 0, but the mutant always returns 0.
For any address that has been minted a non-zero quantity of a token, the balanceOf function must return a value greater than zero; the mutant always returns zero, violating this invariant.
For any account and token ID, after minting a non-zero quantity, the returned balanceOf must equal the minted quantity, but the mutant always returns 0, violating the equality for any non-zero mint.
The balanceOf function should always return the exact stored balance; the mutant adds 1, causing any non-zero-address query to return balance+1.

For any account that is not the zero address and any token id, balanceOf(account, id) must return exactly the stored internal balance of that account for that token id; the mutant adds 1, so it will return a value one larger than the stored balance.
For any non-zero address and any token id, balanceOf(account, id) must return exactly the stored internal balance; the mutant adds 1, so it returns a value one larger than the stored balance.
bug: balanceOf with zero address returns 0 instead of reverting, violating the rule that querying balance with address(0) must always revert

balanceOfBatch must return an array whose length equals accounts.length with every element populated; the buggy version skips alternate indices, leaving zeros for those positions when accounts.length > 1.

For any accounts and ids arrays of equal length, balanceOfBatch must return an array where every index i (0 <= i < accounts.length) holds the balance of accounts[i] with respect to ids[i], but the buggy mutation leaves zeros at every second index.

For any input arrays, the length of the returned batchBalances array must equal the length of the ids array; the buggy version can return a shorter array when accounts is shorter than ids, breaking the invariant.

For any admissible inputs, balanceOfBatch must return an array of the same length as the accounts array; the buggy version can return a longer array when ids is longer than accounts, breaking this invariant.

For any inputs, if balanceOfBatch succeeds, the returned array's length must equal both input array lengths; the buggy version succeeds with mismatched lengths, leading to a returned array whose length differs from the ids array length.

balanceOfBatch must return an array of the same length as the input arrays, with the last element equal to the balanceOf the last account/id pair. The mutant leaves the last element as zero, breaking this rule.

For any non-empty input arrays of equal length, the number of non-zero entries in the output of balanceOfBatch must equal the number of non-zero balances among the queried (account, id) pairs; the mutant leaves the last entry always zero, violating this count for inputs where the last pair has a non-zero balance.
balanceOfBatch must return a result where the last element equals the balance of the last queried (account, id) pair; the mutant leaves it as zero, violating this.
balanceOfBatch must return a result array whose last element equals the balance of the last account-id pair; the mutant leaves that element zero.
balanceOfBatch must return the correct balance for every account in the input arrays; the mutant skips index 0, leaving the first returned balance as the default 0 instead of the actual balance.

balanceOfBatch must return a correct, non-zero balance for every account when a valid non-zero balance exists; the mutant leaves the first element as zero when accounts and ids have length >= 1 and the first account holds a non-zero balance.
For any non-empty accounts array, balanceOfBatch must return the actual balance for every account (including index 0), but the mutant leaves the first element uninitialized (0) for that index.
balanceOfBatch must return correct balances for all provided accounts, but the mutant leaves the first element uninitialized (zero) when accounts has exactly one element.
Balance-of-batch for a set of accounts and tokens must equal the sum of each per-account per-id balance, but the mutant always returns zero for every entry.

For any valid inputs where accounts and IDs have equal length, the value returned by balanceOfBatch at each index must equal the result of a separate balanceOf call for the same account and ID; the mutant breaks this because it always returns 0 instead of the actual balance.

For any accounts and ids arrays of equal length, the returned batchBalances array must be non-empty when accounts is non-empty, and the mutant's zero return violates this by producing an array of zeros regardless of actual balances.

For any accounts and IDs of equal length, the sum of balanceOfBatch entries must equal the sum of individual balanceOf calls for each (account, id) pair; the bug returns all zeros, so the sum is zero unless all actual balances are zero.

For any equal-length arrays of accounts and token IDs, balanceOfBatch returns an array whose entries sum to the same total as the sum of individual balanceOf queries, but the mutated version always returns zeros, so the sums differ whenever any balance is positive.

The length of the returned array from balanceOfBatch always equals accounts.length; the buggy version can return an array of lengths other than accounts.length when ids.length differs (which the fuzzer can make happen by sending arrays of equal length).

The returned array from balanceOfBatch must have exactly the same length as the input `accounts` array, and the buggy version can return a shorter array when `ids` is shorter than `accounts` (which satisfies the equal-length precondition) because it iterates only up to `ids.length`.

For any accounts and ids of equal length, the returned array length always equals accounts.length, but the buggy version returns an array of length ids.length (which equals accounts.length only when the fuzzer provides equal-length arrays) so this property always holds for the reference and always holds for the mutant when lengths match, thus never distinguishes. The actual difference: when accounts.length == ids.length but the arrays have different data, the reference processes all elements up to accounts.length while the mutant uses ids.length (which equals accounts.length) so they iterate same count; no length mismatch observable. The only observable difference is when the loop bound differs from the array allocated size — but allocation uses accounts.length, so if ids.length < accounts.length the mutant writes fewer elements leaving trailing zeros; if ids.length > accounts.length it writes out-of-bounds (silently to memory after the array). The bug can cause return data corruption when ids.length > accounts.length. The general rule: for any equal-length inputs, the returned array elements at each index i correspond exactly to balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for all i < accounts.length. The mutant violates this when ids.length > accounts.length by writing beyond the array bounds into return data.

For all equal-length accounts and ids with ids.length < accounts.length, the returned array's last accounts.length - ids.length elements must be initialized to the default zero balances for the remaining accounts, but the mutant iterates only ids.length times, leaving those suffix elements as the default zero balances of the allocated memory, which happens to be zero; however, when ids.length > accounts.length, the reference correctly processes all accounts.length elements, while the mutant iterates ids.length times and writes beyond the allocated batchBalances array, corrupting return data; the general rule is: the balanceOfBatch output length must be exactly accounts.length, and the mutant will produce a return data blob whose length does not match the declared expectation when ids.length > accounts.length, causing the call result to appear corrupted or padded.

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, the return data of balanceOfBatch must contain exactly accounts.length balance values; the mutant violates this when ids.length > accounts.length by writing beyond the allocated array, corrupting the returned bytes.

The isApprovedForAll function must return the actual operator approval status set via setApprovalForAll; the mutant always returns true, so after an owner revokes approval the function incorrectly reports true.
